name: SiteSuperCharger
author: AnAdminer

sections.description:
SiteSuperCharger helps your website look as attractive as possible to search engines helping you to acheive the highest search engine rankings.

Contact Marketing Heroes (https://www.mheroes.com) to get started!
sections.installation:
Install SiteSuperCharger via the plugin directory, or by uploading the files manually to your server. After activating SiteSuperCharger, you’ll need to enter your GUID at Settings -> SiteSuperCharger

For info about acquiring a GUID for SiteSuperCharger visit https://www.mheroes.com.
sections.faq:
Is SiteSuperCharger free?

You must purchase Search Engine Optimization services from Marketing Heroes (https://www.mheroes.com) to use SiteSuperCharger
sections.changelog:
5.6.5

Release date: TBD

  • Fix: ShortPixel “Drift” status persisted permanently on fleet sites because the plugin-side hash and the SSC-app-side hash were computed over different structures (the plugin used a nested two-section dict with no prefix; the app used a flat dict with a sha256: prefix). Resync would not clear the warning even when settings were in fact synchronized. The plugin now reconstructs the dict in the exact key order received from /api/sites/{guid}/shortpixel-config, JSON-encodes via the same canonical shape, and prefixes sha256: — matching the app hash byte-for-byte. Drift detection now reflects real divergence (e.g. hand-edits to ShortPixel options outside the SSC sync path).
  • New: AI Image SEO Prompt is now visible inside the SSC Speed-tab card alongside the existing sync state rows. Previews the first 200 characters with a “View full” expander for the complete prompt. Customers no longer need to ask staff to confirm which AI prompt is in play on a given site.
  • Internal: voice-composite per-PBN-site prompt storage scaffolded (wp_options key ssc_voice_composite_prompt, admin row on the Advanced tab). No external behavior change yet — downstream content-generation wire-up ships in a follow-up release.

5.6.3

Release date: TBD

  • Fix: fleet-wide ShortPixel settings drift root cause — the ssc_heartbeat_tick action (which fetches the standard ShortPixel profile + AI context + org-wide API key from the SSC app and applies it to local ShortPixel options) had been registered as an add_action handler since v5.5.7 but was never scheduled with wp_schedule_event, so the sync ran zero times across the fleet. Heartbeat now scheduled hourly with a per-site offset based on the site GUID to spread the load on the app endpoint.
  • Fix: enable_ai (master AI switch on ShortPixel) was missing from the Pattern B settings map, leaving AI tagging inconsistent across fleet sites even when explicitly enabled in the app-side standard profile. Now included in the sync.
  • New: org-wide ShortPixel API key push (Pattern C). The API key is authored once in the SSC app’s API Settings and pulled by the plugin from /api/sites/{guid}/shortpixel-config (response field api_key) into the serialized spio_key WordPress option that the ShortPixel plugin reads. The API key is no longer stored in plugin code — rotating it app-side propagates to every fleet site on the next heartbeat tick.

5.6.2

Release date: TBD

  • Fix: customer blog posts with AI-generated titles containing non-ASCII characters (curly apostrophe, em-dash, etc.) failed to land their featured images during sideload, leaving blog content with no hero image. Filenames are now sanitized via WordPress’s sanitize_file_name() before write. Affects content generated since the v5.5.35 SEO-rename change.
  • Fix: legacy SEO-rename-on-upload filter disabled — was the surface that introduced the non-ASCII filename bug. Standard WP sanitize_file_name is sufficient for ASCII safety.
  • Internal: idempotency backstop on downloadImage for hand-recovered attachments — augments the existing v5.6.0 _ssc_image postmeta check with an attachment_url_to_postid lookup so that attachments restored by manual rsync (e.g. APC May-8 recovery) are reused rather than duplicated on subsequent re-sync.
  • Fix: customer hero images failed to sideload from app.sitesupercharger.com on sites whose _ssc_image postmeta cache was empty or stale — IIS origin was returning HTTP 406 Not Acceptable on image probes because the plugin sent Accept: application/xml. Image probes now use Accept: */* to match the asset content type. This is the root cause for the 2026-05 TruPro/Creative/RMH/TVS missing-hero-image incident.
  • Internal: remoteFileExists now logs the actual HTTP status code on any non-success response and the WP_Error message on transport failures, so future silent-skip incidents diagnose in minutes instead of hours.
  • Fix: createPost featured-image binding no longer writes a null _thumbnail_id postmeta when the underlying downloadImage call returns falsy — adds !empty() guard mirroring the existing post-update branch.

  • Garza scheduler support: new PublishPost SiteCommand handler. Plugin reads the post payload embedded in the dispatch params and inserts a published WordPress post. Coordinated with app-side PublishScheduledPostsJob (PR #1076 commit e2b3a9cc).

5.5.29

Release date: Apr 26th, 2026

  • Self-enabling auto-updates: SiteSuperCharger now auto-updates itself from wp.org by default. Previously, WordPress required admins to manually opt-in to plugin auto-update per-plugin in the admin Plugins screen, and on most managed sites that opt-in was never flipped — so sites stagnated on whatever version they last received. Starting with this release, the plugin tells WordPress “yes, auto-update me” via the standard auto_update_plugin filter. Site admins who genuinely need to pin a specific version can disable this by defining SSC_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE in wp-config.php. Other plugins on the site are unaffected — they still follow whatever the site admin has configured.

5.5.28

Release date: Apr 25th, 2026

  • Plugin Settings now shows the Site GUID and the SSC app URL on the Overview tab, with click-to-select formatting — no more hunting through wp_options to find the GUID for a support ticket.
  • New “Sync now” button on the Overview tab: pulls the latest config from the SSC app immediately instead of waiting for the next 5-minute cycle. Useful right after changing settings in the SSC app.
  • Auto-purge on save: when a page or post is published or updated, that single URL is purged from the Cloudflare cache automatically so the next visitor sees fresh content. Throttled to one purge per URL per 30 seconds so block-editor save-revise loops don’t spam Cloudflare. Goes through the new credential-pass-through proxy when proxy mode is enabled, so no CF token has to live on the WordPress site for this to work.
  • New token-mismatch warning: if the SSC app starts rejecting this site’s API token (because it was rotated in the SSC app and not updated here), a loud red “API token mismatch” card appears on the Overview tab so admins can fix it before settings sync, command polling, and health reporting all silently break.
  • Sitemap status card now shows “SEO plugin detected” before “HTML sitemap display” — the upstream context appears first.
  • Security tab AI Crawler Policy is now a radio-button list with a one-paragraph plain-English description per option (instead of a tiny dropdown). Choosing the right policy no longer requires reading the docs. New “View live robots.txt” link opens the rendered file in a new tab so admins can verify the policy took effect.
  • Lead-conversion tracking for Gravity Forms, Contact Form 7, WPForms, and Formidable Forms: successful submissions now fire a GA4 generate_lead event automatically. Closes the form-conversion gap that previously required MonsterInsights Pro.
  • Cloudflare connection card on the Security tab: paste a Cloudflare API token to connect a site whose domain isn’t already linked in the SSC app. The token is forwarded directly to the SSC server, encrypted at rest, and stored there — it is never written to this WordPress site.
  • New security policy applied site-wide: any non-public credential the SSC app sends down (e.g. Cloudflare API token) is now stripped from the local cache before storage. The plugin asks the SSC server to perform credential-bound actions (cache purge, etc.) instead of holding the key itself.
  • New “Export URLs” card on the Sitemap tab: download a CSV of every published URL on the site (pages, posts, and any public custom post types). Columns include post type, ID, title, status, last-modified date, and whether the URL is SSC-managed. Replaces the separate “Export All URLs” plugin.
  • Plugin audit rules: Edit Author Slug now flagged as redundant for security (SiteSuperCharger already blocks ?author=N and the /wp-json/wp/v2/users REST endpoint); Malcure Malware Shield documented as a complement to SiteSuperCharger’s drift-hash + spam quarantine; Export All URLs flagged as redundant once the new built-in export ships.
  • Save buttons across the v6 admin UI now use a cloud-upload icon (matching the standard rolled out across SiteSuperCharger this week).
  • Manual “Purge this page from Cloudflare” button on the post and page edit screens (Publish meta box). Complements the auto-purge on save for cases where you want to clear the edge cache without re-saving.
  • Daily health-grade-drop email digest: when a site’s overall SiteSuperCharger health grade drops a letter (A → B, B → C, etc.), the admin gets an email with the failing checks. No spam on recoveries or same-grade ticks. Disable per-site by setting the wp_option ssc_health_alert_enabled to 0.
  • New “Recent activity” card on the Overview tab: surfaces the last 5 audit-log events inline so admins see what SiteSuperCharger has been doing without leaving the page.
  • Maintenance buttons redesigned: each maintenance action (Rebuild content, Check duplicates, Clear cache – all pages, Clear cache – SSC only, Check for plugin update) now appears as a label-and-description row with a real button on the right, instead of full-card “panels” that didn’t read as clickable buttons.
  • Health tab: new blue “How to reach a perfect score” guidance bar (only shown when grade < A) listing the most common gaps in plain language — Trust Badges, Claim Responses, Tracking IDs, AI Crawler Policy, Redirects.
  • Redirects tab: inline “Add redirect” form replacing the old “click a link to classic admin” flow. Fields for from URL, to URL, HTTP code, and an optional note. Reloads on save to show the new entry.
  • Tracking tab: replaced the placeholder “coming soon” panel with a real vertical list of every tracking ID this plugin emits (Facebook Pixel, GA4, GTM, Google Ads, Consent Mode v2). Each row shows whether it’s configured and the actual value where applicable. Custom head/footer scripts (when set) are previewed in a code block so admins can see exactly what’s being injected.
  • Schema tab: new “Current schema values” card showing how many trust badges and ClaimReview entries are configured (with the first one’s name as a sanity check), plus a one-click button to open Google’s Rich Results test pre-filled with this site’s home URL.

  • Slug-collision fix on landing-page sync: when SiteSuperCharger creates or updates a landing page and another post is already holding the desired URL slug (admin-created page, leftover from a prior install, or a stale draft), WordPress used to silently append -2 to the new page — producing pages like /shingle-roof-installation-2/ and breaking the canonical URL. SiteSuperCharger now detects the collision and reclaims the slug: stale SiteSuperCharger pages with mismatched IDs are moved to Trash (recoverable), admin-created pages get their slug renamed to <slug>-admin-<ID> so the human’s content is preserved but the canonical SiteSuperCharger URL is freed. Audit log entries are written for each reclaim. Closes the kangaroof ~12% landing-page-404 issue.
    Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • Daily file-integrity check: SiteSuperCharger now records a fingerprint of every plugin/theme/core file once a day and reports any unexplained changes back to the admin app. Catches tampering and silent file corruption that ClamAV alone wouldn’t notice.

  • Bundles every fix and feature from 5.5.22 through 5.5.26 (cumulative release).

5.5.26

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • WooCommerce purchase tracking in Google Analytics 4: product views, add-to-cart, checkout-started, and completed purchases all flow into GA4 automatically — no separate plugin needed. Includes a duplicate-event guard so refreshing the thank-you page never inflates revenue numbers.

5.5.25

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • New [ssc-howto] shortcode for service landing pages: produces a step-by-step instruction list with the search-engine schema markup that Google uses for HowTo rich results.
  • Redundant-plugin nudge: when SiteSuperCharger now covers something a separately installed plugin used to do (for example MonsterInsights, Insert Headers and Footers, the Cloudflare official plugin), the admin sees a one-time, dismissible notice on activation pointing them to the SiteSuperCharger setting that replaces it.

5.5.24

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • Spam blog-post quarantine: backlink-spam posts (casino / pharma / payday-loan patterns) are auto-moved to Trash and an email is sent to the admin. Nothing is ever permanently deleted — every action is recoverable from Trash.

5.5.23

Release date: Apr 24th, 2026

  • Google Consent Mode v2: tracking pixels (Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, Google Ads) now start in a privacy-respecting “denied” state and only upgrade to full tracking when the visitor accepts cookies through your consent banner. Compatible with CookieYes, Complianz, Cookiebot, and any banner that uses the standard gtag('consent','update') signal — or a simple ssc_consent=granted cookie for banners that can’t.
  • Google Ads remarketing / conversion tag: enter a Google Ads ID in tracking settings and the AW- conversion tag is injected automatically.

5.5.22

Release date: Apr 23rd, 2026

  • Closed two account-enumeration leaks: the /wp-json/wp/v2/users REST endpoint and the /wp-json/wp/v2/settings endpoint are now hidden from anonymous visitors. Logged-in editors and admins still get normal access. Companion to the existing ?author=N block — together they stop the most common username-harvesting probes used against WordPress.
  • Admin improvements.

5.5.21

Release date: Apr 23rd, 2026

  • Plugins tab: inline Delete button on orphan plugin folder rows. Server revalidates the target against a fresh orphan scan before deleting — arbitrary paths are rejected. Requires delete_plugins capability and per-action nonce. Every attempt is written to the audit log (plugin.orphan_deleted / plugin.orphan_delete_failed / plugin.orphan_delete_rejected).
  • Plugin audit rules expanded per plugin-scoping DECISIONS.md:
    • DANGER (REMOVE-WITH-WARNING): Object Cache Pro, WP Rocket, NitroPack, WP Super Cache — all conflict with SSC’s Cloudflare edge caching. WP phpMyAdmin Extension — direct DB access security risk.
    • WARN (REMOVE): Jetpack, BlogVault, WPMU DEV Dashboard — unnecessary on SSC-managed sites.
    • INFO (ALREADY-COVERED — redundant with SSC): Disable Comments, Activity Log, Cloudflare (official).

5.5.20

Release date: Apr 23rd, 2026

  • Plugins tab: severity-tiered audit alerts (danger/warning/info) flag dangerous, conflicting, duplicate, and orphaned plugin installs with a summary banner + per-row chips.
  • Orphan plugin directory scanner surfaces .disabled, .old, .bak, .pre-*, and .orig leftover folders under wp-content/plugins.
  • Plugin audit results piggyback on the daily heartbeat so the app sees fleet-wide audit state.
  • Plugins tab “Updated” column shows month + 2-digit year (e.g. Apr '25) for clarity across release years.
  • Sitemap tab: merged XML sitemap + provider rows into a single row with the full URL, removed non-functional toggle button.

5.5.17

Release date: Apr 22nd, 2026

  • Hourly Site Health report: each site automatically sends its plugin / WordPress / PHP version, content totals, Cloudflare status, and any plugin conflicts back to the admin app — fleet-wide health visible at a glance, no manual logins required.
  • Expected-content cross-check: the plugin asks the admin app how many pages, blog posts, and FAQs the site is supposed to have, so missing or extra content is caught early.
  • Remote command channel: a small 5-minute cron picks up admin-initiated commands (purge cache, refresh settings, push health, run an incremental rebuild) without anyone having to log into the site.
  • Richer Article rich results: featured images on blog posts are now described to Google with their actual width and height — improves how posts appear in search results and Google Discover.
